query: For the paper "Sign Language Recognition Analysis using Multimodal Data" (arXiv: 1909.11232), answer this question: What are the deep learning architectures used?

drafts: The paper's proposed architectures are an RNN architecture with a novel spatial data augmentation technique, and an architecture that uses both RGB and skeletal data to improve recognition accuracy [3]. It also employs LSTM networks, described as an architecture with an internal memory maintained via gates [13]. In its literature review, the paper additionally mentions Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and three-dimensional CNN used with RGB video data [6].

This architecture is referred to as long short term memory (LSTM) network [24].

Huang et al. [2] demonstrated the effectiveness of using Convolutional neural network (CNN) with RGB video data for sign language recognition. Three dimensional CNN have been used to extract spatio-temporal features from video [3].

cited_sources.text: In summary, the contributions of this work are: • We propose an RNN architecture with a novel spatial data augmentation technique. • We propose an architecture which uses both RGB and skeletal data to improve recognition accuracy. • We introduce and publicly release a multi–modal dataset for ASL called GMU-ASL51. II. LITERATURE REVIEW Most sign language recognition systems use RGB video data as input. These approaches model sequential dependencies using Hidden Markov Models (HMM).

Huang et al. [2] demonstrated the effectiveness of using Convolutional neural network (CNN) with RGB video data for sign language recognition. Three dimensional CNN have been used to extract spatio-temporal features from video [3]. Similar architecture was implemented for Italian gestures [10].

This architecture is referred to as long short term memory (LSTM) network [24]. While the basic RNN is a direct transformation of the previous state and the current input, the LSTM maintains an internal memory and has mechanisms to update and use that memory. This is achieved by deploying four separate neural networks also called gates. Figure 4 depicts a cell of an LSTM network which shows input at the current time step xt and the previous state ht−1 enter into the cell; and get concatenated.
